title: W-14: the response-header cap is only enforced when the terminator is missing
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-14 (low). readHead concatenates the chunk, finds the terminator, and checks size only in the else branch, so a 17 KB header block arriving in one chunk is accepted despite the 16 KiB limit, and body bytes arriving with it are copied into the retained buffer, contradicting the comment and ADR 0009. Output stays status-only. Files: src/adapters/https-transport.ts, src/domain/destination.ts, ADR 0009.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The size boundary is checked before a header block is accepted and total buffered bytes are bounded
The head is copied out so no body suffix is retained
The comment and ADR 0009 are reworded: TLS buffers can receive bytes past a logical parser boundary
Tests cover an oversized single-chunk head and a head with coalesced body bytes
